blocks.text: Ezekiel 17 presents a cryptic riddle using the imagery of two great eagles and a vine to communicate a message about Judah's relationship with imperial powers. After presenting the riddle, Ezekiel himself offers interpretation, beginning in verse 12, connecting it directly to the Babylonian conquest of Jerusalem and the removal of Judah's leadership.

The prophet identifies the first eagle as the king of Babylon. According to the passage, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, seized the king and princes, and carried them to Babylon, establishing a covenant and requiring oaths of loyalty. This historical reality reflects Judah's fall to Babylon, when its temple and king were removed as part of the exile—a profound covenant crisis for a small kingdom living under persistent imperial pressure.
